messages:
alex: incident-bot just paged me — we're seeing a surge of model fetch failures from Hugging Face when instances try to cold-start new models. errors are 429/503 from hf artifact endpoints. logs: ```ERROR fetching model manifest from https://huggingface.co/api/models/{repo}/resolve/main/config.json -> 429 Too Many Requests
stack: model_fetcher.go:142 -> downloader.go:77 -> runtime_init.go:51```

incident-bot: [INCIDENT] hf-artifact-rate-limit - automated detection: >5% fetch failures over 10m for hosted runtime across us-west-2, severity: P1. Pager duty: ops_pager. See incident playbook link: https://rwd.internal/playbooks/hf-artifact

mira: seeing identical 429 spikes across multiple model families, mostly large-checkpoint and LoRA variants. Prefetch cache hit rate dropped from 72% -> 18% in last 12m. cold starts skyrocketing.

samir: quick customer-impact check: hosted inference requests are returning 502/504 after model load timeout for ~12% of requests to endpoints serving newly requested model versions. No data-plane integrity issues — inference containers that already have KV cached are fine.

jess: flagged in product slack: a few mid-market customers reported errors in their health dashboards. Not yet a widespread customer alert but we should prepare an outbound if this persists >30m. 

alex: action plan proposal: 1) throttle model rollout traffic, 2) disable automatic on-demand fetch for non-critical models, 3) enable internal artifact mirror fallback, 4) bump retry/backoff and circuit-breaker to avoid hammering HF. who can implement mirror fallback now?

infra-bot: rolling patch queued to change fetch backoff to exponential with randomized jitter (base=1s, max=30s) across runtime pool. Patch id: rwd-rt-3482. Applying to canary (10% traffic) now.

mira: I can push a config change to canary: set `artifact.fetch.retry_policy=exponential_jitter(base=1s,max=30s,attempts=5)` and `prefetch.enabled=false` for non-critical models. Applying in 2m.

oncall-bot: @ops_pager assigned — escalation in 5m if errors not reduced. Current metrics: fetch_fail_rate=0.18, cold_start_p99=3.2s -> 9.9s, active_rollouts=14.

ops_pager: I'm on it. First step: stop new canary rollouts and pause scheduled model pulls. Pushing pause to control plane now: `POST /admin/rollouts/pause` -> 200 OK.

samir: started internal mirror failover path — if hf fetch returns 429/503, try internal mirror host `artifacts.internal.rwd.co` which has replicas for commonly used open models. Mirror contains quantized variants too. We're redirecting reads there for 99 models initially.

alex: Mira + Samir, coordinate to ensure mirror uses same integrity checks (sha256) before allowing runtime to boot model. We can't risk silent corruption.

mira: verified checksums for mirror replicas for the first 99 models. checksum pipeline ✅. Switching 10% of cold-starts to mirror now via routing policy change.

jess: customer comms draft: "We're investigating intermittent model load failures caused by a third-party artifact host (Hugging Face). Some requests may experience higher latency or transient errors while we failover. We'll update in 30 mins or once mitigated." Want approvals before sending.

sre_lead: approve. Add note about mitigation (mirror fallback + increased backoff). Keep messaging high level. Ops_pager: send at 15m if still unresolved.

ops_pager: HF support ticket created: https://huggingface.co/support/tickets/324512 (internal ref HF-2026-03). Reached out via enterprise channel; awaiting response. Provided request logs and rate-limit headers.

samir: quick patch to runtime: if HF returns `X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0` or 429, increase retry delay to `min(max_delay, header_reset_seconds + 1s)` to respect vendor rate limits. Rolling this to canary.

mira: canary metrics after 7m: fetch_fail_rate down from 0.18 -> 0.06; cold_start_p99 improving 9.9s -> 6.1s. Mirror traffic at 10% and stable. Prefetch disabled for low-priority families.

alex: good. next: disable non-production mirrors to reduce accidental churn, and enforce per-tenant throttles so a single tenant doesn't cause mass cold-starts. Samir can you draft tenant throttle change?

samir: drafting `tenant.cold_start.rate_limit=1/min` for free-tier, `3/min` for standard customers, adjustable via console. Will push as feature flag `tf-tenant-throttle`.

oncall-bot: Handoff triggered: @ops_pager -> @mira at 1800000000 (30m). Please ack.

mira: ack taking handoff. I'll monitor mirror saturation and HF support reply. If HF remains rate-limited beyond 45m, we escalate to contingency: 1) promote smaller quantized variants for affected deployments, 2) open emergency customer status page.

jess: drafted status page update in staging. Waiting for greenlight. Also recommend outbound to top 10 customers now (email + CSM pings) since they saw errors.

ops_pager: agreed. Sending targeted email to top 10 now. Logged outreach in ticket HF-2026-03.

incident-bot: detected HF enterprise channel reply: "We've throttled public artifact endpoints due to abnormal request patterns; enterprise customers should use token-authenticated artifact downloads. We're investigating." Timestamped 17m after ticket creation.

alex: that's useful. We should confirm whether our runtime uses token-authenticated requests for enterprise customers. If not, rotate to token auth for those tenants to bypass public throttle.

samir: confirmed: our enterprise deployments already use token-authenticated HF registry. The affected failures are coming from anonymous fetches from hosted ephemeral instances for public models. Workaround: require token for all fetches and rate-limit per-key. Implementing token-enforcement for new fetches in 10m.

mira: metrics after token enforcement + mirror failover: fetch_fail_rate -> 0.02, cold_start_p99 -> 4.0s, overall request error rate for affected endpoints down to 2.1%. 

jess: sent customer emails to top 10 and posted concise status update on status.redwood.ai: "Partial model load failures due to third-party artifact rate limits; mitigation in place (mirror + auth). Some endpoints may still see elevated latency; targeted customers notified." 

sre_lead: recommend we keep incident open for 4 hours for postmortem and retro. Add action items: 1) build more robust global mirror for top 500 models, 2) vendor SLA negotiation with HF for artifact throughput, 3) improve pre-warm logic to avoid mass concurrent fetches, 4) feature-flag to enforce token-auth for new models.

mira: adding retro items to triage board. Creating follow-up ticket RWD-RT-3991 with owners: mira, samir, jess, alex. ETA for mirror scale plan: 2 weeks.

ops_pager: closing pager escalation. Will remain monitoring for 2 hours. If HF reopens public endpoints before then, we'll revert some of the rate-limiting conservations. 

alex: thanks everyone — excellent coordination. Final note for postmortem: include timeline, customer impact numbers (approx 12% affected at peak, top-10 customers proactively contacted), and cost of mitigation (mirror egress + engineering time). We'll schedule postmortem doc in #postmortems and a follow-up on the incident channel.

mira: copying logs and saved dashboards to the incident ticket. Marking thread resolved draft in 1h pending HF final confirmation.

oncall-bot: thread auto-note: handover completed at 1800000000, incident state: mitigated -> monitoring. 

samir: closing comment — consider long-term: prefetching quantized variants during low traffic windows to reduce dependence on third-party during spikes. noted in RWD-RT-3991.
